newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon readies three-year t-bills - source.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon readies three-year t-bills - source.

text.p: Lebanon is preparing to issue three-year treasury bills in a few weeks, following the recent rapid fall in interest rates on existing treasury bills, banking sources said on Tuesday.
"It is a very serious project, but the decision will be taken by the finance ministry," a banker told Reuters. "I figure it won't take a long time. I would guess within a few weeks."
Lebanon currently issues three-month, six-month, 12-month and two-year treasury bills at a weekly auction. The bills are the government's main source of funds for financing the public debt.
"The idea was to wait until the yield curve was more advantageous, and as you see, there has been quite a sharp drop in interest rates lately," the banker said.
T-bill rates have dropped rapidly in the past two months, and Beirut dealers said they expected the downward trend to continue at a slower pace.
Yields, which ranged in mid-November from 14.44 percent for three-month bills to 21.42 percent for two-year bills, now range from 14.08 percent to 17.14 percent.

The banking source said the yield on three-year bills would have to be linked to the two-year rates. Another banker said he expected three-year yields to be between 1.5 percent and two percent above the two-year rates.
